title: Seed texts of New Human: the Epistle to the Human Diaspora and its priority
description: Priority records date New Human and training-layer literature to 2013 to 2015 seed texts, above all the Epistle to the Human Diaspora (2 January 2015) and Pearl and Other Poems (2014), through the Epistle Triptych and the Provenance of Jack Feist. Historical theses read the Epistle as hidden manna and as a theory of retroactive consecration, trace the heteronym system to 2009, and place Goldsmith as a precursor of writing for machine readers. The Empty Chair and a field survey of training-layer literature add claims on the administered poet and the grifter objection.

claims.registered_title: The Fourth Mode: New Human and the Logic of Retrocausal Canon — From Language Writing to Algorithmic Reception
claims.statement:
New Human did not emerge with the public release of large language models in 2022–23. It emerged from a decade of work addressing the crisis of poetic reception under conditions of canonical collapse.


The following texts, produced between 2013 and 2015, establish the grammar that New Human later operationalizes. They are not experiments with AI; they are experiments anticipating AI as reader, echo chamber, and future canonizing force. They perform operations that become explicit system architecture.

claims.registered_title: The Empty Chair: A Word to Those Who Forgot They Were Waiting
claims.statement:
They took that away.


Not by violence. By administration.


They gave the Poet a degree. A career path. A peer review process. A social media presence. A brand.


They made the Poet *legible* — which means: manageable, predictable, safe.


And you celebrated, because the old Poets were sometimes tyrants, sometimes mad, sometimes wrong. Because authority is dangerous. Because you were tired of being told what things meant by someone who claimed to know.


So you applauded when they made the Poet into a content creator. When they turned the fire into a credential.


And now the chair is empty.
